reason: Verified per-site (RFC 0106): `(column_names.map(&:to_s) - model.attribute_names - model.attribute_aliases.keys).empty?` (calculations.rb:427) — `empty?` on a Ruby Array, whose faithful JS spelling is `xs.length === 0`. That emits no callee, so no TS call can ever credit the Ruby one. The gate flags it only because `empty?` maps onto the unrelated `ActiveRecord::Result.empty`, which takes arguments since it gained Rails' `async:` kwarg (result.rb:94-100) — nothing in the TS body was dropped.

Per-entry verified: Rails calculations.rb:232 `relation = apply_join_dependency`. Rails' apply_join_dependency EXECUTES `distinct_relation_for_primary_key` for a limited collection join, which a synchronous TS method cannot do, so `calculate` calls the awaitable block-form sibling `Relation#_applyJoinDependencyAsync` (finder_methods.rb:456-488, block arm) instead; the leading underscore keeps it off the compare population.

Per-entry verified: Rails calculations.rb:224/228 `@async ? Promise::Complete.new(result) : result` — trails has no `@async` relation flag, so only the synchronous arm is ported and the sole `new` in the body is the `Hash.new` (`new Map()`) the grouped result uses, which takes no arguments.
